First, the bad news...
According to the latest FEC reports, we were outraised last quarter by our extreme far-Left opponent, Angie Craig. She raked in 2.5 million bucks from her army of mega-donors and political connections. She now has nearly 5 million dollars on hand to drag my name through the mud and lie about what I believe in.
Luckily, there's good news too:
It was close. Very close. We raised more than all our Republican opponents combined and finished up just shy of far-Left Angie Craig. I was proud of that - especially since I launched my campaign part of the way through the quarter!
The far Left is panicking for a reason. They know they're already on thin ice, having covered up unprecedented fraud in Minnesota, opening our borders to anyone and everyone, and crushing us with taxes and high costs.
America is fighting back. And Minnesota is ground zero.

My mother was quite fond of the adage that "those who cannot remember the past are condemned to repeat it." Coined [either](https://substack.com/redirect/46f6bd99-8c22-473a-8089-71d873879ce5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Spanish-American philosopher George Santayana, Anglo-Irish philosopher Edmund Burke, or British statesman Winston Churchill, it indicates the importance of history as a tool to educate the present in order, one hopes, to enable a brighter future.
In retrospect, her death in 2016 at the hands of cancer may have been a blessing. If her illness hadn't driven her to her grave, the daily outrages invited by life under the current president would have likely done that, instead. She passed at a moment in history when the illusion of progress seemed more plausible, before the ensuing decade, for so many of us, irrevocably shattered that confidence.
Today offers a fitting reason to recall the past, particularly since decades of widespread ignorance have enabled a continuing series of horrifically stupid decisions that are actively destroying the future we all share.
_Thanks for reading Chronicles of a Dying Empire! You can help inform your friends by sharing this post on any social media sites that you use._
[ Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1018597&post_id=197926681&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk3OTI2NjgxLCJpYXQiOjE3Nzg4OTAzNDgsImV4cCI6MTc4MTQ4MjM0OCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTEwMTg1OTciLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.YLPej8ePb8AuSxPDtIllSj_wCXuMgpaKUSnWZ6ZsQ74)
### **An annual commemoration rarely acknowledged in the West**
May 15 commemorates [Nakba Day](https://substack.com/redirect/ce41fd13-cc6e-4346-b107-1d91df643b68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and the forced expulsion of Palestinians from their ancestral homeland by Zionist terrorists in the 1940s.
When the Israeli genocide targeting Gaza accelerated in 2023, many of us struggled with how to convey the longstanding pattern preceding that. It behooves readers unfamiliar with the documented history to explore the roots of today's conflict. As painfully [explained](https://substack.com/@rashaaboujalal1/note/c-259403842?r=97w99) by Rasha Abou Jalal:
> More than 750,000 Palestinians were forcibly uprooted from their cities and villages and turned into refugees inside and outside their homeland. Zionist militias, followed later by the Israeli army, destroyed more than 530 Palestinian towns and villages, wiping entire neighborhoods off the map while committing dozens of massacres that forced people to flee in fear for their lives.
> The Nakba was not only the theft of land, but an attempt to uproot the Palestinian people from their memory, identity, and right to life itself....
> Today, as Palestinians commemorate the Nakba, the people of Gaza are living through another chapter of the same tragedy. Since October 2023, more than two million Palestinians have been subjected to forced displacement under bombardment, siege, and starvation, with entire families repeatedly fleeing in search of safety that does not truly exist.
> The scenes lived by grandparents in 1948 are being repeated today before the eyes of the world...children sleeping in tents, and cities reduced to rubble. The only difference is that today the world watches everything unfold live, in sound and image.
> The Nakba did not end in 1948. It continues in different forms to this day....
### **A continuing history suppressed for too long**
Nakba Day is a fitting day to remember this widely suppressed history, particularly in the wake of a [recent (and long overdue) report](https://substack.com/redirect/c3dd03f5-09a6-45e3-b0a8-7e711f21f5ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in The New York Times documenting the use of torture and rape by Israel against Palestinian civilians, including women and children. (The article is also available on [other sites](https://substack.com/redirect/408d8a30-20e9-43b3-bdbc-1d347db09c2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that do not require a paywall)
The report is nightmarish, but it behooves every person of conscience to grapple with the terrifying reality of human rights abuses routinely committed by Israel with bipartisan support from Washington:
> Palestinians have recounted...a pattern of widespread Israeli sexual violence against men, women and even children -- by soldiers, settlers, interrogators in the Shin Bet internal security agency and, above all, prison guards....
> [Israeli leaders] have built a security apparatus where sexual violence has become, as a United Nations report [put it last year](https://substack.com/redirect/f4fea09b-c106-470d-91a4-a017ba790fa5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), one of Israel's "standard operating procedures" and "a major element in the ill treatment of Palestinians." A [report out last month](https://substack.com/redirect/b6b5d72a-ad42-4074-8edd-587cad5b7912?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), from the Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor, a Geneva-based advocacy group...concludes that Israel employs "systematic sexual violence" that is "widely practiced as part of an organized state policy."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b10992f1-a728-4922-8d6e-afd8d8f20393?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The cover of the Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor to which Kristof linked in his revealing NYT article
What Nicholas Kristof documents is frankly horrifying, but even more horrifying is the disturbing reality that these abuses have been going on for years, enabled by support from Washington in which [both of America's fascist political parties](https://substack.com/redirect/cebb84f5-dd51-40ee-9f44-2ac243666843?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) have been thoroughly complicit--even to [their own detriment](https://substack.com/redirect/d86b8dd9-a92f-4867-826d-d83c35dbdf19?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
### **There is more to this tragic --and continuing--story**
I hope to write at further length in the coming days to explore more layers to this story, including:
* how Israeli propaganda has long dominated American "news" media
* how the U.S. has long followed a path similar to that taken by Israel more recently
* how Americans have been among the casualties of Israeli belligerence
* how the struggle to define history has sparked everything from lawsuits and direct action to wars and regime change
* how the Nakba continues today through the ongoing Israeli genocide in Gaza
* how the Israeli genocide in Gaza relates to the economic collapse unfolding across the U.S. invited by Netanyahu & Trump's unprovoked war on Iran

While I hope to explore those topics in my next post, I wanted to make sure this one got finished in time to publish today, before I head to work. Thanks to all the subscribers who support my writing and allow me the privilege to focus some of my time on these crucially important issues!

name: Crystal & Jason via ActionNetwork.org
subject: News from the Front Lines: Pipeline Resistance, Rights of Nature & Upcoming Fundraisers
body:
Let's have some fund with mini golf and a guessing game while we are fighting fossil fuel expansion, organizing for Rights of Nature, and building community support across North Carolina. | | | News from the Front Lines
## 7 Directions of Service Community Newsletter
As fossil fuel infrastructure rapidly expands across North Carolina and the Southeast, 7 Directions of Service continues to stand on the front lines of environmental justice, Indigenous sovereignty, and community protection. Our organizing is grounded in relationship-building, cultural revitalization, and the creation of long-term shifts toward Indigenous visions of justice, sustainability, and collective care. Through coalition-building across race, class, and geography, we continue working to create healthy, affordable, and just communities for future generations.
## Fighting Fossil Fuel Expansion
Our Fossil Fuel Team remains actively engaged in resistance efforts against major infrastructure projects, including:
* Transco’s Southeast Supply Enhancement Project (SSEP)
* Mountain Valley Pipeline Southgate Extension
* New gas plants and fossil fuel buildout tied to hyperscale data centers
* Duke Energy’s expanding gas infrastructure plans

Currently, construction related to SSEP is affecting land, forests, waterways, and communities in Rockingham, Guilford, and Forsyth Counties as pipeline installation continues across the region. At the same time, we are organizing around emerging threats associated with massive data center expansion and the growing energy demands that are fueling new fossil fuel infrastructure across North Carolina. From Stokes County to Chatham County, 7 Directions of Service continues to build strong, multi-racial, cross-class coalitions rooted in environmental justice and Indigenous leadership.
## Rights of Nature Organizing Across North Carolina
As we prepare to lobby for Rights of Nature legislation again in February 2027, our team is traveling across North Carolina to educate towns, counties, organizations, and community members about the Rights of Nature movement. Through workshops, presentations, community conversations, and coalition-building, we are helping communities imagine legal systems that recognize the inherent rights of rivers, ecosystems, and the natural world to exist, flourish, and regenerate.
## Community Fundraisers Supporting the Movement
As grassroots organizers, we know that sustaining this work requires community support. To help offset funding gaps and build long-term sustainability, we have several upcoming fundraisers and community events.
### The Great Guessing Jar Fundraiser
📅 May 16 – June 16, 2026
Try your luck and support Indigenous-led environmental justice work by participating in our community guessing game fundraiser! 🎟 Participate Here:
[The Great Guessing Jar Fundraiser](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.xqm-apKpWqGuZCDDu9wrxQJvqq150s7idT6evB1GRadGPB3V3AGJG4QB5FLyEQg5WOb7hhwYxU-dzfLO6dxqYu5MfnYJj8YeuoiyfMGgK_GC5BlhRgytm-xrwRI0jeSe-hhGxROj9JaHTYc44wXUUjbRpyoRaojICrHjKzEuG9Ps6_70eKxtxaCfnWiaKB5Q5-5cfI8KPcVVhNQRCi4vSzi1gVVVKTSiZHJx9QvEvwE2-J9hxDYf0yz48rA-Um6lYPVFDeeXJB8aMJaHNWV0KVo4rRDvUXaXk966zyLzlIygH53ArtU7f8Uly48YpO_qV5TeTdzzs2wt7vUf7sjnFWd53PlJr88akopEO8CPm2Q/4qo/IFfBZTWOT664jdYp06_YtQ/h0/h001.p_uUPJLNKDSXRgEBXHk3qouo3AFZfMkNFJh7Mu3INRU)
### Putting for People, Water, and Land
⛳ Mini Golf Fundraiser In Pleasant Grove
📅 Sunday, July 19, 2026 @ 1:45 PM EDT Join us for a fun-filled afternoon of mini golf, raffles, prizes, community connection, and fundraising in support of Indigenous-led environmental justice, youth programming, traditional ecological knowledge, and community wellness initiatives. ### Rooted in Motion Virtual 5K
📅 June 26 – July 3, 2026 Rooted in Motion is a virtual movement challenge supporting:
* Indigenous-led environmental justice initiatives
* Cultural revitalization programs
* Youth leadership
* Food sovereignty efforts
* Community healing work

Participants can join from anywhere by walking, running, biking, hiking, paddling, rolling, or moving in ways that are accessible to them. This event is designed to be inclusive, family-friendly, community-centered, and accessible to people of all ability levels. 🎟 Register Here:
[Rooted in Motion Virtual 5K](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.X6XUC7u8ppFLNtMO_55SZhC1Z9oS-UN3IQX48ADMBk0CKraH3diUasfDmKSRwfYZdEhTJsSXfBu0fQWDVYEe3orCTr2Ta5ybI_LE1fKrNQlmXJ5JkBzrMtIxusrSr5Qkq5PIMjJcujHFbpBijdwN9qR6DIE05OJHAlwofE8VY7zNVG6Evx6Fb8NhNhJaDpkVHCHXTNAhTewWAPCZmdFGCMKQZ-y5WIQ6Cyxv1IoBTcVIJyef8VfnDDIBY214DZ09GpempHzRhg6rBTcNuZywCriw3wAgPvHV49oVq3n1ySmcP9kHjq1a81kgd5OYU0iupV0XVO2IvoJUPjqw26MJDpX8oY7yy2trkGmEVfnIabA/4qo/IFfBZTWOT664jdYp06_YtQ/h2/h001.60EULkQIuM7aNvn-XVaJgE92-aIGKd372hF86Zekrxk)
### Silent Auction Fundraiser
📅 July 10 – August 10, 2026 We will also be launching an online Silent Auction featuring community donations, local businesses, Indigenous artists, gift baskets, experiences, and more. Stay tuned for additional details and ways to participate! Together, we continue building a future rooted in justice, healing, and collective care. With gratitude,
Crystal & Jason

name: Kat Abughazaleh
subject: Coming to you for your support at a difficult time
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JUSTICE DEMOCRATS
body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Hi Peter, this is Kat Abughazaleh.

I’m the journalist and researcher who recently ran for Congress in
Illinois’ 9th district with the help of Justice Democrats. We didn’t win
our primary, but thanks to grassroots momentum from people like you,
neither did AIPAC’s candidate.

I’m coming to you now to ask for your support again at a difficult time.

In October 2025, I – along with my field director and friend Andre Martin
and four other individuals – was indicted for my advocacy and protest
against ICE and the Trump administration.

[ https://www.gofundme.com/f/stand-with-kat-and-andre-against-unjust-prosecution?utm_source=jd-em-20260515-2 ]Image of Andre Martin and Kat Abughazaleh sitting in protest holding
two poster signs; Andre's sign says 'ICE/CPB HIRING OF MORE FASCISTS TO
ASSAULT CHICAGO? HELL NO!'; Kat's sign says: 'IMMIGRANTS ARE WELCOME HERE.
FASCISTS AREN'T'

Even though we plan on winning, the two of us are facing up to $250,000 in
legal debt, along with the immense stress and pressure the last six months
has put on us and our loved ones. Yes, that is how much cases like this
can cost — and honestly, it’s at the low end of the spectrum, especially
for two separate incredible legal teams.

But that’s the point of lawfare like this: for the government to be able
to scare us into silence through not just possible jail time but financial
and psychological torture.

Our case, United States v. Rabbitt, is set to go to trial in Chicago
federal court on May 26, and the result could determine the future of our
constitutional right to free association. These charges are bogus, but
regardless of the outcome, the stress, public scrutiny, and financial
burdens of this ordeal have forever changed our lives.

Throughout my congressional campaign, I was not just vocal against Donald
Trump's secret police — I put my body and reputation on the line during
protests. Even if you don’t know my face, you probably saw the video of an
ICE agent throwing me to the ground last September. That is not what we
were charged for, but it shows what the conditions at Broadview were often
like for protestors.

As we have said from the beginning, dissent and protest are not a
conspiracy. After lengthy legal battles, the government dismissed the
felony conspiracy charge just weeks before trial. But they did not dismiss
all the charges, and we still have trial on the misdemeanor counts for
intimidating, interfering, and impeding an ICE agent. And by winning our
case, we can give future defendants a path to victory, ensuring no one
else has to go through this without precedent.

Since Andre and I have worked in the nonprofit sector and progressive
politics our entire adult lives, we don’t have hundreds of thousands (much
less mere thousands) of dollars to spare. The costs have mounted beyond
our expectations.

Even if – or rather, when – we win our trial, our lives and futures will
still be left in disarray through the financial and psychological burdens
of our legal system.

We didn’t win our primary, but thanks to grassroots momentum from people like you, neither did AIPAC’s candidate. I’m coming to you now to ask for your support again at a difficult time. In October 2025, I – along with my field director and friend Andre Martin and four other individuals – was indicted for my advocacy and protest against ICE and the Trump administration. [ ]Image of Andre Martin and Kat Abughazaleh sitting in protest holding two poster signs; Andre's sign says 'ICE/CPB HIRING OF MORE FASCISTS TO ASSAULT CHICAGO? HELL NO!'; Kat's sign says: 'IMMIGRANTS ARE WELCOME HERE. FASCISTS AREN'T' Even though we plan on winning, the two of us are facing up to $250,000 in legal debt, along with the immense stress and pressure the last six months has put on us and our loved ones. Yes, that is how much cases like this can cost — and honestly, it’s at the low end of the spectrum, especially for two separate incredible legal teams. But that’s the point of lawfare like this: for the government to be able to scare us into silence through not just possible jail time but financial and psychological torture. Our case, United States v. Rabbitt, is set to go to trial in Chicago federal court on May 26, and the result could determine the future of our constitutional right to free association. These charges are bogus, but regardless of the outcome, the stress, public scrutiny, and financial burdens of this ordeal have forever changed our lives. Throughout my congressional campaign, I was not just vocal against Donald Trump's secret police — I put my body and reputation on the line during protests. Even if you don’t know my face, you probably saw the video of an ICE agent throwing me to the ground last September. That is not what we were charged for, but it shows what the conditions at Broadview were often like for protestors. As we have said from the beginning, dissent and protest are not a conspiracy. After lengthy legal battles, the government dismissed the felony conspiracy charge just weeks before trial. But they did not dismiss all the charges, and we still have trial on the misdemeanor counts for intimidating, interfering, and impeding an ICE agent. And by winning our case, we can give future defendants a path to victory, ensuring no one else has to go through this without precedent. Since Andre and I have worked in the nonprofit sector and progressive politics our entire adult lives, we don’t have hundreds of thousands (much less mere thousands) of dollars to spare. This is how campaigns used to be run, and I think it is how they should still be run, because you deserve a candidate who puts in the work and is willing to lose some sleep before they ask for your vote. **My intention isn 't to make it to Capitol Hill and disappear, I'm committed to listening to every voice! **Saturday, May 16, at 6 pm PT / 9 pm ET**[**In person at Casa Latina in Seattle, or over livestream**](https://kshamasawant.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7ef0e21448b54140a81773aff&id=bfa3a1d0b0&e=bbdb764b3a)

| | Kshama’s campaign for the U.S. Congress is fighting for:👉 The right of Puerto Rican people to self-determination👉 Cancel the Puerto Rican debt - make Wall Street pay👉 Abolish Puerto Rican tax haven laws for the rich👉 Free healthcare for all in the U.S., including in Puerto Rico - tax the rich
---
|
---
| | **Kshama will be joined by community organizers and members of the Puerto Rican independence movement in the diaspora.**

**We will have pastries catered by**[**Seattle-based Puerto Rican restaurant, Mi Patria**](https://kshamasawant.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7ef0e21448b54140a81773aff&id=0e16a5f267&e=bbdb764b3a)**!**
**Speakers include:**
* Kshama Sawant
* Jenaro Abraham (Assistant Professor of Political Science, Gonzaga University/incoming professor at San José State University; Vice President of the Puerto Rican Independence Party in the Diaspora)
* Alejandro Tañón (Secretary of Youth Affairs, Puerto Rican Independence Party in the Diaspora)

---
| | Dear Peter,
For working people to win any improvements in our living standards, we need to build national and international solidarity on a working-class basis. That also means that working people in the 50 states of America and the working people of Puerto Rico need to get united and fight together against the same billionaire class!
Working people in Puerto Rico have a long history, since the late 1800s, of facing colonization, oppression, and exploitation at the hands of the American and Western capitalist class.
Since Puerto Rico was invaded by American military forces in 1898, the American ruling class has used the island as its personal military and financial playground. This has meant a proliferation of American military bases, resource grabs by the wealthy, and 120 years of impoverishment and economic devastation of the people of Puerto Rico.
The impact of neocolonialism, neoliberalism, and capitalism as a whole are all too evident today. Puerto Rico faces a horrific poverty rate of over 43 percent — nearly 60 percent of children live in poverty.
In the wake of the powerful Hurricane Maria in 2017, Puerto Rico’s agriculture, industry, and electricity and other infrastructure were left in complete disarray. The American billionaires and multimillionaires saw this as an opportunity to make yet another killing.
The billionaire class rapidly privatized the island's publicly owned power grid, transferring operations to profit-making companies like LUMA Energy and robbing the Puerto Rican working class and poor by indiscriminately raising electricity rates.
With many new laws nakedly favoring the ultra rich, Puerto Rico has increasingly been used as a wealth tax haven for billionaires like crypto-investors.
All of this is reminiscent of how working and poor people in Louisiana were exploited in the wake of the 2005 Hurricane Katrina, and how working people nationally were sold out in the aftermath of the 2008 Great Recession, while both Bush and the Republicans and Obama and the Democrats bailed out the Wall Street owners.
In a stunning example of adding insult to injury, the Puerto Rican people have now been left with a crippling $70 billion of debt!
As a revolutionary socialist, Kshama supports the call for Puerto Rican working people’s right to independence from the United States and self-determination. Tragically, the leadership of the vast majority of left organizations in the United States have not taken a meaningful stand against this.
---
|
---
| | Kshama’s campaign for the U.S. Congress is fighting for:👉 The right of Puerto Rican people to self-determination👉 Cancel the Puerto Rican debt - make Wall Street pay👉 Abolish Puerto Rican tax haven laws for the rich👉 Free healthcare for all in the U.S., including in Puerto Rico - tax the rich
---
|
---
| | This Saturday, May 16th at 6pm at Casa Latina, we invite you to come out in person or over the livestream to be a part of an important discussion on how to fight for these demands, and why Kshama’s campaign and the fight to elect her to Congress are so crucial to this fight.
The liberation of the Puerto Rican people cannot be achieved on the basis of capitalism. And we cannot achieve socialism in just one country.
The struggle for self-determination must be combined with the struggle for socialism in Puerto Rico, in the United States, in all of Latin and North America, and internationally.
This struggle must include the fight for immediate demands such as canceling all debt for working and poor people in Puerto Rico, free healthcare funded by taxing the rich, and good union jobs for all.
Our campaign is excited to be a part of this discussion with the Puerto Rican community, and we encourage anyone to attend in person at Casa Latina tomorrow, Saturday, May 16th at 6pm!
Solidarity,Kshama for Congress

Ballots have already been in Californians’ hands for over a week—**and people are making decisions _right now_ about who’s going to fight for them.**
Last night, Katie joined the final debate before the June 2 election. She made it clear who this campaign is for: _working Californians getting crushed by rent, groceries, health care costs, and a political system that keeps siding with corporations and billionaires._
Now, the real fight is making sure undecided voters actually hear her message before they turn in their ballots.

**[Peter, can you chip in $5 right now to help us break through to voters while there’s still time?](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20260515_3_ak.bt7nHZ&refcode=em20260515-41362&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=41362%2E3422442%2EuJRTTl)**

subject: Judicial Watch Asks Court to Unseal NIH Royalty Payments
body:
Judicial Watch Challenges EPA’s $2B Stacey Abrams Grant

[INSIDE JW]

JUDICIAL WATCH ASKS COURT TO UNSEAL ROYALTY PAYMENTS TO NIH EMPLOYEES

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=81559&L=37853&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g/dj1ObHQ2TERYbWpLYyZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=abbbd3d126ab980a784743de96616051b97123fc0ed531dc3c9505287b920da1]

As they say, follow the money. That’s what we’re doing with
government employees making decisions about your health. We want to
see how much private companies pay federal health bureaucrats, but
they’re fighting back.

We filed a
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=81559&L=37854&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2FtZXJpY2FuLXRyYW5zcGFyZW5jeS12LWhocy1zdXAtYnJpZWYtMDI4MjEvXXBvc3QtaGVhcmluZz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=ab739467f0fc462b515c536b28ae1ffce4304a2fdfcf2ae001218f72beaa23b7
brief
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=81559&L=37838&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2FtZXJpY2FuLXRyYW5zcGFyZW5jeS12LWhocy1zdXAtYnJpZWYtMDI4MjEvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=b670a531e30622acf910a2a305e31d5c7bd5df79ded0e13d6caddd667a128f78]
in a lawsuit on behalf of Open the Books urging a federal court to
compel the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to release unredacted
records showing royalty-related payments to government scientists,
including former National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases
(NIAID) Director Dr. Anthony Fauci.

Our October 2021Freedom of Information Act (FOIA)
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=81559&L=37855&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvanctc3Vlcy1uaWgtcm95YWx0aWVzL11sYXdzdWl0P3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=60fbd48c8ec27ee4305891990aa502ca1e1be9de208079a17908e495a0910981
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=81559&L=26601&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvanctc3Vlcy1uaWgtcm95YWx0aWVzLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=c52c6e8dc5a6d923b4df3e7b07343b6b422737f9c9fe82ce237e3b1475901c5e] seeks full
disclosure of NIH “Inventor Award” payments—compensation issued
to federal employees for taxpayer-funded inventions licensed to
private companies.

We argue that the NIH has improperly withheld these records based on
speculative claims that disclosure could allow outsiders to
“back-calculate” confidential royalty payments made by private
industry to the government.

In a March evidentiary
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=81559&L=37856&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2FtZXJpY2FuLXRyYW5zcGFyZW5jeS12LWhocy10cmFuc2NyaXB0LTAyODIxL11oZWFyaW5nP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=fc9f36b6a81d5cefeedc0273eaaa3f0f2c553682773170174d23235241179293
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=81559&L=37839&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2FtZXJpY2FuLXRyYW5zcGFyZW5jeS12LWhocy10cmFuc2NyaXB0LTAyODIxLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=de23f3f129f58d72c9f812621244e14c473078161bdbe928461d7bafa553b16a]
before US District Court Judge Amit Mehta, NIH witnesses attempted to
justify redactions by arguing that releasing inventor payment amounts
could reveal private-sector royalty rates.

We
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=81559&L=37857&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2FtZXJpY2FuLXRyYW5zcGFyZW5jeS12LWhocy1zdXAtYnJpZWYtMDI4MjEtcGdzLTItMy9dY29udGVuZD91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=a79fe565c26dbc8fd0ddc88df68388f9f9ec32f5dc66d4feee740f22f274ee1c
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=81559&L=37840&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2FtZXJpY2FuLXRyYW5zcGFyZW5jeS12LWhocy1zdXAtYnJpZWYtMDI4MjEtcGdzLTItMy8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=8f77329b3a464fb5aa3dba2fd0ff6d7aeeeba56ff262aa27a9864eba0a258f25]
that the government’s argument is based on unrealistic hypotheticals
rather than actual data:

> The evidentiary hearing was Defendant’s opportunity to prove that
> Inventor Awards could be used to back calculate royalty amounts. Of
> the 59,000 instances in which NIH redacted Inventor Awards ... it
> did not back calculate a royalty payment from a single award.
> Instead, it offered on direct examination what appeared to be actual
> examples from 1985.... It became clear on cross examination,
> however, that the examples were not real instances of Inventor
> Awards and a royalty amount ... but only hypotheticals. Dr. Kirby
> testified on cross examination that she “made up” the numbers
> ... She also testified that the numbers were “all arbitrary
> numbers that [she] selected.” ... Because it was only a
> hypothetical based on arbitrary numbers, Dr. Kirby did not have a
> real-life royalty amount against which to check her work.

In our brief, we argue that there are too many unknowns and moving
parts for anyone to reliably “work backwards” to those private
payments. The system is too complicated to figure out how much private
companies paid the government just by looking at what scientists were
later paid – or to guess:

> [National Institutes of Health] witnesses failed to establish that
> back calculation is possible for any of the withheld Inventor
> Awards. Cross examination made clear that the agency’s witnesses
> offered only grossly simplified hypotheticals, not actual royalty
> amounts back calculated from actual Inventor Awards paid to real NIH
> employees and withheld from Plaintiff. These hypotheticals were
> devoid of the many variables—known only to NIH and perhaps the
> relevant licensee ...

We are asking the court to order the release of the responsive,
unredacted NIH “Inventor Award” records, arguing they are being
unlawfully withheld.

Taxpayers have a right to see how money from taxpayer-funded
inventions is distributed. Judicial Watch and Open the Books already
forced disclosure of more than $1 billion in NIH royalty payments
marked to inventors, like Fauci. It is head-scratching that HHS
Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. would allow this stubborn and unlawful
secrecy to continue about payments to Fauci and others.

“Americans have a dual interest in the disclosure of these
payments,” said Open the Books CEO John Hart. “Every taxpayer
deserves to understand how private payments may impact decision making
among public scientists and agency directors. Equally important, they
are patients making some of life’s most personal decisions when it
comes to health care. They are entitled to understand all the
financial stakes in play as they receive guidance from public health
officials.”

In earlier rulings in the case, Mehta rejected the NIH’s effort to
broadly shield the royalty program using employee privacy claims,
writing that “federal government employees have a limited privacy
interest in information concerning their compensation.”

The court also emphasized the strong public interest in disclosure,
noting that transparency regarding royalty payments could help the
public assess whether inventors’ financial interests in licensed
technologies “could potentially bias the design, conduct, or
reporting of clinical research.” Mehta further concluded that the
public interest in understanding these financial arrangements is
significant, particularly where government scientists involved in
taxpayer-funded biomedical research may receive payments tied to the
commercialization of those technologies.

Over $2.685 billion
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=81559&L=37283&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cub3BlbnRoZWJvb2tzLmNvbS9hc3NldHMvMS82L05JSF9Db3JydXB0aW9uX2FuZF9Db25mbGljdF9GSU5BTC5wZGY/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=580734367868395df71ecc356fc0694a1b1447bc6378b2891bc739f75b329938]
was paid to NIH institutes or scientists – of which more than $1
billion was marked for inventors – between 2010-2023 from
pharmaceutical companies and other private entities licensing
government-owned patents. Those payments were obtained only after
Judicial Watch and Open the Books forced the NIH to release previously
hidden royalty payment records through FOIA litigation.

The disclosures include royalty payments connected to inventions
developed across multiple NIH institutes, including the National
Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), which was led
for decades by Fauci and played a central role in federally funded
biomedical research.

In February, we filed a separate FOIA
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=81559&L=37858&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2FtZXJpY2FuLXRyYW5zcGFyZW5jeS12LWhocy1uaWgtcm95YWx0aWVzLWNvbXBsYWludC0wMDQzMi9dbGF3c3VpdD91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=134e6a5270ce52edea49b766f963c86a48b8b93bdb2451e0547ccb29b0f6b1ad
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=81559&L=37284&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2FtZXJpY2FuLXRyYW5zcGFyZW5jeS12LWhocy1uaWgtcm95YWx0aWVzLWNvbXBsYWludC0wMDQzMi8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=eff94fdb9188200ec2e6ea1be41ab31a6057bde437d2da81e4de089d223a7d46]
on behalf of Open the Books seeking records concerning whether
statutory limits on royalty payments to federal employees are being
effectively bypassed (_American Transparency v. U.S. Department of
Health and Human Services_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=81559&L=37285&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2FtZXJpY2FuLXRyYW5zcGFyZW5jeS12LWhocy1uaWgtcm95YWx0aWVzLWNvbXBsYWludC0wMDQzMi9dXz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=0345c48be82ae105e8a05c3575c0c44399e507b01c973cb7a11f21f559a8e0f6 _(No.
1:26-cv-00432)).

That lawsuit seeks records including:

* Emails referencing royalty payments that may exceed the statutory
cap
* Records concerning royalty payments placed in reserve when payments
exceed statutory limits
* Internal guidance and procedures governing the NIH Public Health
Service Technology Transfer Policy Manual

> The records requested cover the period January 2020 through December
> 2025.

Federal law limits the amount individual government employee-inventors
may receive in royalty payments to $150,000 per year. NIH scientists
may receive royalty payments when inventions developed with taxpayer
funding are licensed to private companies. These payments originate
from license fees paid by pharmaceutical companies and other entities
seeking to commercialize government-developed biomedical technologies.

OpenTheBooks.com [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=81559&L=26165&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cub3BlbnRoZWJvb2tzLmNvbS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=38495a7ceb7164eed1dee36b7c2ff83a1d54e1ca6b16b7cf0106a9483e777018], operated by American
Transparency, maintains one of the largest independent databases of
public-sector spending in the United States, promoting transparency by
putting government spending records online for public review.

JUDICIAL WATCH SUES EPA OVER BIDEN’S $2 BILLION GRANT TO STACEY
ABRAMS

As the Biden administration was collapsing in 2024, it lawlessly
rushed out billions in cash to left-wing interest groups in a way that
encouraged fraud and abuse. We’re suing to help expose this.

We filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit against the
Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) for records of the Biden
administration’s $2 billion Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund grant to
the nonprofit Power Forward Communities, which is tied to failed
Georgia Democratic gubernatorial candidate Stacey Abrams (_Judicial
Watch Inc. v. U.S. Environmental Protection Agency_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=81559&L=37845&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZXBhLWdyZWVuaG91c2UtZ2FzLXJlZHVjdGlvbi1mdW5kLWNvbXBsYWludC0wMTYzOC9dXz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=09a62ad4cfcd18735c05efe0a47e3c46115d30e251d0c384241f153989f4e2ab _(No.
1:26-cv-01638)).

The taxpayer funds, awarded in April 2024, were from the $14 billion
National Clean Investment Fund program established under the Biden
administration’s massive Inflation Reduction Act. The grant was
awarded to finance so-called “residential decarbonization.”

Power Forward Communities, which was established in 2023, is a
coalition of nonprofits which includes partners like Rewiring America,

clean_body: Judicial Watch Challenges EPA’s $2B Stacey Abrams Grant [INSIDE JW] JUDICIAL WATCH ASKS COURT TO UNSEAL ROYALTY PAYMENTS TO NIH EMPLOYEES [] As they say, follow the money. That’s what we’re doing with government employees making decisions about your health. We want to see how much private companies pay federal health bureaucrats, but they’re fighting back. We filed a [ brief [] in a lawsuit on behalf of Open the Books urging a federal court to compel the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to release unredacted records showing royalty-related payments to government scientists, including former National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) Director Dr. Anthony Fauci. Our October 2021Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) [ [] seeks full disclosure of NIH “Inventor Award” payments—compensation issued to federal employees for taxpayer-funded inventions licensed to private companies. We argue that the NIH has improperly withheld these records based on speculative claims that disclosure could allow outsiders to “back-calculate” confidential royalty payments made by private industry to the government. In a March evidentiary [ [] before US District Court Judge Amit Mehta, NIH witnesses attempted to justify redactions by arguing that releasing inventor payment amounts could reveal private-sector royalty rates. We [ [] that the government’s argument is based on unrealistic hypotheticals rather than actual data: The evidentiary hearing was Defendant’s opportunity to prove that Inventor Awards could be used to back calculate royalty amounts. Of the 59,000 instances in which NIH redacted Inventor Awards ... it did not back calculate a royalty payment from a single award. Instead, it offered on direct examination what appeared to be actual examples from 1985.... It became clear on cross examination, however, that the examples were not real instances of Inventor Awards and a royalty amount ... but only hypotheticals. Dr. Kirby testified on cross examination that she “made up” the numbers ... She also testified that the numbers were “all arbitrary numbers that [she] selected.” ... Because it was only a hypothetical based on arbitrary numbers, Dr. Kirby did not have a real-life royalty amount against which to check her work. In our brief, we argue that there are too many unknowns and moving parts for anyone to reliably “work backwards” to those private payments. The system is too complicated to figure out how much private companies paid the government just by looking at what scientists were later paid – or to guess: [National Institutes of Health] witnesses failed to establish that back calculation is possible for any of the withheld Inventor Awards. Cross examination made clear that the agency’s witnesses offered only grossly simplified hypotheticals, not actual royalty amounts back calculated from actual Inventor Awards paid to real NIH employees and withheld from Plaintiff. These hypotheticals were devoid of the many variables—known only to NIH and perhaps the relevant licensee ... We are asking the court to order the release of the responsive, unredacted NIH “Inventor Award” records, arguing they are being unlawfully withheld. Taxpayers have a right to see how money from taxpayer-funded inventions is distributed. Judicial Watch and Open the Books already forced disclosure of more than $1 billion in NIH royalty payments marked to inventors, like Fauci. It is head-scratching that HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. would allow this stubborn and unlawful secrecy to continue about payments to Fauci and others. “Americans have a dual interest in the disclosure of these payments,” said Open the Books CEO John Hart. “Every taxpayer deserves to understand how private payments may impact decision making among public scientists and agency directors. Equally important, they are patients making some of life’s most personal decisions when it comes to health care. They are entitled to understand all the financial stakes in play as they receive guidance from public health officials.” In earlier rulings in the case, Mehta rejected the NIH’s effort to broadly shield the royalty program using employee privacy claims, writing that “federal government employees have a limited privacy interest in information concerning their compensation.” The court also emphasized the strong public interest in disclosure, noting that transparency regarding royalty payments could help the public assess whether inventors’ financial interests in licensed technologies “could potentially bias the design, conduct, or reporting of clinical research.” Mehta further concluded that the public interest in understanding these financial arrangements is significant, particularly where government scientists involved in taxpayer-funded biomedical research may receive payments tied to the commercialization of those technologies. Over $2.685 billion [] was paid to NIH institutes or scientists – of which more than $1 billion was marked for inventors – between 2010-2023 from pharmaceutical companies and other private entities licensing government-owned patents. Those payments were obtained only after Judicial Watch and Open the Books forced the NIH to release previously hidden royalty payment records through FOIA litigation. The disclosures include royalty payments connected to inventions developed across multiple NIH institutes, including the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), which was led for decades by Fauci and played a central role in federally funded biomedical research. In February, we filed a separate FOIA [ [] on behalf of Open the Books seeking records concerning whether statutory limits on royalty payments to federal employees are being effectively bypassed (American Transparency v. U.S. Department of Health and Human Services [ (No. 1:26-cv-00432)). That lawsuit seeks records including: Emails referencing royalty payments that may exceed the statutory cap Records concerning royalty payments placed in reserve when payments exceed statutory limits Internal guidance and procedures governing the NIH Public Health Service Technology Transfer Policy Manual The records requested cover the period January 2020 through December 2025. Federal law limits the amount individual government employee-inventors may receive in royalty payments to $150,000 per year. NIH scientists may receive royalty payments when inventions developed with taxpayer funding are licensed to private companies. These payments originate from license fees paid by pharmaceutical companies and other entities seeking to commercialize government-developed biomedical technologies. OpenTheBooks.com [], operated by American Transparency, maintains one of the largest independent databases of public-sector spending in the United States, promoting transparency by putting government spending records online for public review. JUDICIAL WATCH SUES EPA OVER BIDEN’S $2 BILLION GRANT TO STACEY ABRAMS As the Biden administration was collapsing in 2024, it lawlessly rushed out billions in cash to left-wing interest groups in a way that encouraged fraud and abuse. We’re suing to help expose this. We filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit against the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) for records of the Biden administration’s $2 billion Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund grant to the nonprofit Power Forward Communities, which is tied to failed Georgia Democratic gubernatorial candidate Stacey Abrams (Judicial Watch Inc. v. U.S. Environmental Protection Agency [ (No. 1:26-cv-01638)). The taxpayer funds, awarded in April 2024, were from the $14 billion National Clean Investment Fund program established under the Biden administration’s massive Inflation Reduction Act. The grant was awarded to finance so-called “residential decarbonization.” Power Forward Communities, which was established in 2023, is a coalition of nonprofits which includes partners like Rewiring America, Enterprise Community Partners, and Habitat for Humanity. Abrams [ [] "played a pivotal role" in establishing the group, which in its first few months of operation reported just $100 in revenue. In early 2025, following the start of the second Trump administration, the EPA under Administrator Lee Zeldin ordered grants made via the National Clean Investment Fund be frozen due to an ongoing investigation into what the [ under Zeldin said [] were “serious concerns” that were raised “regarding self-dealing and conflicts of interest, unqualified recipients, and reduced government oversight.” In February 2025, the Trump administration's EPA [ [] it would take steps to get the money back. Zeldin cited comments from a former Biden EPA political appointee, who described disbursements made through the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund as akin to "tossing gold bars off the Titanic," because Biden officials were allegedly trying to get money out the door before Trump took over. In March 2025, the grant payments were halted, while Citibank, the banking entity used to help move or transfer the grants, froze the payments after recommendation from the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). Power Forward Communities was one of several nonprofits that filed a lawsuit against the EPA and Citibank to prevent the termination of the grants and have restored access to the funds. In March 2025, U.S. District Judge Tanya S. Chutkan [ [] a temporary restraining order blocking the EPA from canceling the grants. The judge also blocked Citibank, which holds the money on behalf of EPA, from transferring it to the government or anyone else. On appeal, the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit in September 2025, [ [] that the District Court had abused its discretion in issuing the injunction while ruling jurisdiction for such claims lay with the Court of Federal Claims and not the district court. The appeals court rescinded Judge Chutkan’s injunction and the funds remain frozen as the case is ongoing. We sued after the EPA failed to respond to a February 20, 2025, FOIA request for all documents and communications regarding the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund grant to Power Forward Communities. The Trump EPA team should disclose and expose every single document about this massive Biden corruption scandal. JUDICIAL WATCH SUES FOR FDA COMMISSIONER'S COMMUNICATIONS ON ABORTION DRUG Judicial Watch filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit for records of communications and meetings of the Federal Drug Administration (FDA) commissioner involving the abortion drug Mifepristone (Judicial Watch Inc. v. U.S. Department of Health and Human Services [] (1:26-cv-01546)). We sued in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia after the FDA failed to respond to a February 25, 2026 FOIA request for: All communications sent to, received by, or copied to the Commissioner of Food and Drugs, or to the Commissioner’s immediate office, that concern, refer to, or discuss mifepristone, RU-486, or any generic or branded form of mifepristone approved, regulated, or reviewed by the Food and Drug Administration. * All documents related to any meeting with the Commissioner of Food Drugs where mifepristone, RU-486,or any generic or branded form of mifepristone approved, regulated, or reviewed by the Food and Drug Administration was discussed, including, but not limited to calendar events, calendar invitations, talking points, PowerPoint presentations, written or audio recordings, and post-meeting summaries The request asked that records be provided for the period April 1, 2025, to the present. In response to pressure from pro-abortion activists, the Clinton Food and Drug Administration accelerated approval of the abortion pill in September 2000. Similarly, the Obama and Biden administrations took steps to make the controversial abortion pill more widely available in a way that undermined its “safe” use. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary resigned earlier this month amid friction with the administration. Pro-life advocates had called for his ouster. Makary reportedly [] slow-walked a safety review of the pill, which can be mailed to states that have limited abortion. Makary’s successor will inherit that review and the tricky politics associated with abortion. For decades, Judicial Watch has investigated and exposed the dangers of the abortion pill pushed on pregnant mothers by the Clinton/Obama/Biden operations. The new FDA leadership needs to get its act together quickly, stop providing special treatment for the abortion pill, and ensure transparency to preserve the rule of law and the public health. We have been instrumental in bringing the controversies surrounding the abortion drug to the public’s attention. In October 2024, wet filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit [] on behalf of Advancing American Freedom Foundation against the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) for FDA records concerning approval of the abortion drug Mifeprex [] (Mifepristone, formerly known as RU-486 []) and meetings between senior FDA officials, White House counsel, and foreign actors. In March 2024, Judicial Watch filed [] an amicus curiae (friend of the court) brief in the U.S. Supreme Court in which it argued “the FDA violated its own unambiguous regulation and relied on pretext.... The FDA’s actions in 2016 and 2021 were arbitrary and capricious and violated the Administrative Procedures Act (“APA”).” And, in 2021, using the Covid-19 pandemic as a tool, abortion proponents “sued the FDA to dispense with the REMS [risk evaluation and mitigation strategy] in-person medical visits as a prerequisite for obtaining Mifeprex and permit the drug to be mailed.” Through a FOIA lawsuit Judicial Watch filed in 2023 uncovered [] at least six Mifeprex-related deaths between 2000 to 2002 that were detailed in Health and Human Services records. Records produced to us in September 2023 included an “Annual Report for Mifepristone [ covering the period September 28, 2000, to September 27, 2001, produced by the Population Council/Danco Laboratories, LLC. The summary indicated that during the testing period 32 “adverse events were reported to Danco and reported by Danco to FDA in periodic reports.” (The existence of adverse event reports does not necessarily establish causation.) Of the 32 reported adverse events, two were 15-day reports (the others were not serious and/or not unexpected). One of the 15-day reports was reported as “hemorrhage due to a ruptured ectopic pregnancy and death.” [Emphasis added] The other was reported as “post-abortal parametritis/endometritis, adult respiratory distress syndrome and bilateral pneumonia.” This latter 15-day report and one case where fever was reported represent the total reports on the marketed drug suggesting infection. In addition, one infection was reported in the Population Council’s 200 mifepristone study and one death [Emphasis added] due to clostridium sordelli infection was reported in the Canadian study. JUDICIAL WATCH AFRICA AID AGENCY WHISTLEBLOWER FACES RETALIATION LAWSUIT Rooting out government corruption often requires brave federal employees to take a stand when they discover it. It’s not easy for them, as the experience of one of our whistleblowers illustrates. The U.S. Department of Justice confirmed in a federal court hearing that its investigation of senior officials at the U.S. African Development Foundation (USADF) continues. But one of our whistleblower clients faces a retaliatory lawsuit brought by the agency’s former president. Our whistleblower clients have spent years courageously reporting corruption and misconduct at USADF, sharing information with the USAID Office of Inspector General (OIG), members of Congress, and the Department of Justice. That information has since been borne out by federal criminal charges and damning reports from the Office of Inspector General for U.S. Agency for International Development and the Government Accountability Office. We have been advancing its whistleblower clients’ work through multiple vehicles, including a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) [ [] seeking USADF records related to those allegations. (Judicial Watch Inc. v. U.S. African Development Foundation [ (No. 1:25-cv-02623)). In an earlier [ [] in that case, the DOJ stated publicly for the first time that it and the USAID OIG were investigating possible crimes committed by senior USADF officials. Shortly thereafter, the Justice Department [ [] Mathieu Zahui, the USADF’s chief financial officer, based in significant part on information from our whistleblower clients. Zahui subsequently pleaded guilty to accepting illegal gratuities and making false statements to federal investigators. During a status conference on March 30, 2026 before Judge Reggie B. Walton of the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, the Justice Department [ [] that its investigation of USADF has not ended. Our whistleblower clients continue to work with members of Congress to demand accountability. Senator Mike Lee recently led a coalition of senators [ [] the Department of Justice to expand its investigation and pursue additional prosecutions arising from USADF’s corruption. Congresswoman Anna Paulina Luna has also taken up the cause, [ [] to Attorney General Todd Blanche to request a broader review of fraud, corruption, and whistleblower retaliation involving senior USADF leadership. Congresswoman Luna specifically highlighted the firsthand account of our client, Jasmine Battle, noting that after Ms. Battle raised concerns about misconduct, she was terminated — and now faces civil litigation by former USADF President Travis Adkins in an effort to silence her. That litigation is itself a form of retaliation. As we [ [] in its motion to dismiss filed on Battle’s behalf: Travis Adkins presided over one of the most corrupt federal agencies in recent memory. During his tenure as president of the United States African Development Foundation, the Senate Foreign Relations Committee named him personally as potentially ‘complicit in, corrupt and potentially unlawful practices’ and placed a congressional hold on the agency’s funding. His own chief financial officer pleaded guilty to public corruption for acts that ran through every year of [Adkins’] leadership. Jasmine Battle, a seasoned and well-respected administrative professional, whose career included working with former cabinet-level officials, witnessed this dysfunction firsthand, served as [Adkins’] assistant for seven months in 2022. What she saw troubled her, and she did what conscientious public servants are supposed to do. She reported it to Plaintiff, to the EEOC, and to oversight bodies like Congress. [Adkins], now under a microscope for what occurred during his tenure as president, is seeking to silence her. And now Battle finds herself in a seemingly partisan crossfire because she had the courage to be a whistleblower.” Jasmine Battle did exactly what a public servant should do — she reported corruption and refused to stay silent. Judicial Watch is proud to stand with her and our other whistleblower clients as we continue to pursue full accountability at the US African Development Foundation. TRANSGENDER DAY OF VISIBILITY ON EASTER AMONG BIDEN’S ANTI-CHRISTIAN POLICIES This summer the celebration of America’s 250th birthday will recognize [] the importance of religious freedom. Joe Biden would not have done this, as our Corruption Chronicles_ blog illustrates []. A governmentwide anti-Christian effort launched under the Biden administration was much worse than previously imagined, and a new report [] published by a Department of Justice (DOJ) task force documents the alarming details of woke measures adopted by most federal agencies to conduct the mission that clearly targeted conservatives. This includes the Biden DOJ mandating the adoption of gender ideology throughout the federal government, illegally weaponizing a landmark civil rights law prohibiting sex-based discrimination to allow men into women’s sports and intimate facilities, punishing faith-based homeless service providers who raised concerns about biological men entering women-only shelters and allowing federally-funded schools to facilitate “gender transitions” without disclosing education records to parents. In 2024 the Biden administration delivered a sucker punch on Good Friday, a solemn and sacred day for Christians, by announcing that Easter Sunday, a Christian holiday celebrating the resurrection of Jesus Christ, would be officially recognized by the government as Transgender Day of Visibility. The flagrant examples go on and on with an extensive list of anti-Christian measures that even President Trump probably could not imagine when he signed an executive order [] in early 2025 to right the wrong. The order created a special Task Force to Eradicate Anti-Christian Bias within the DOJ to protect the religious freedoms of Americans by ending the anti-Christian weaponization of the government. “The Founders established a Nation in which people were free to practice their faith without fear of discrimination or retaliation by their government,” Trump’s order states, adding that the previous administration engaged in an egregious pattern of targeting peaceful Christians while ignoring violent, anti-Christian offenses. The task force uncovered the Biden administration’s radical policy agenda and documented cases in detail in the recently issued 200-page report, which includes over 300 pages of exhibits and evidence illustrating how individual federal agencies discriminated against Christians. Besides the DOJ, they include key agencies such as the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), the departments of Education, Housing and Urban Development (HUD), Health, and Human Services (HHS) as well as Homeland Security. Examples of the “systemic culture” of anti-Christian bias include the FBI collaborating with the leftwing extremist group Southern Poverty Law Center (SPLC) to investigate, track and scrutinize Catholics who were wrongly labelled “potential violent extremists or domestic terrorists” based on their views on abortion, immigration, human sexuality and their preferred popes. A 2023 FBI memorandum included in the report asserts that “radical-traditionalist” Catholics are domestic-terrorism threats and suggests infiltrating Catholic churches as “threat mitigation.” The DOJ criminally charged numerous peaceful pro-life Christians for praying and demonstrating outside abortion facilities. Among those charged and slapped with multi-year prison sentences was a Catholic priest, an 87-year-old woman, a 75-year-old grandmother and a father of 11 arrested after praying and singing hymns outside an abortion facility in Tennessee as part of a politically motivated persecution campaign by the Biden administration. HHS, which is responsible for enhancing the health and well-being of all Americans, took multiple steps to discriminate against Christian families over their religious beliefs because Biden officials viewed their values as harmful to children with gender dysphoria or same-sex attraction. The agency prevented foster children from being placed with Christian families or Christian foster agencies that did not affirm the Biden administration’s policies on sexual orientation and gender ideology. The Department of Education issued excessive fines against Christian universities, pushed policies in which men were allowed into girls’ locker rooms and promoted ideological materials about gender identity to young children that fundamentally conflict with Christian tenets. The agency also allowed federally funded schools to facilitate gender transitions without disclosing education records to their parents. HUD made participation in its housing programs conditioned on compliance with the administration’s woke gender identity nondiscrimination requirements even if they conflicted with a provider’s religious beliefs. Federally managed museums on the National Mall forced pro-life students participating in a peaceful demonstration to remove religious and pro-life attire or leave the premises and the National Park Service twice denied a Catholic organization access to a national cemetery where it planned to hold a quiet Memorial Day mass to honor fallen soldiers. “As our report lays out, the Biden Administration’s actions devastated the lives of many Christian Americans,” acting Attorney General Todd Blanche, Chair of the Task Force to Eradicate Anti-Christian Bias, said in a statement []. “The Department of Justice will continue to expose bad actors who targeted Christians and work tirelessly to restore religious liberty for all Americans of faith.” Blanche confirms that no American should live in fear of being punished by their government for their faith. subject: I’m Already Fighting for Oregon Communities
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Danielle Bethell PAC 20220 [Preferences](https://daniellebethell
body:
While other candidates talk about leadership, I’ve been doing the work.
[](https://daniellebethell.cmail19.com/t/y-l-auldrut-hhlrhljhit-r/) Friends,This week, Marion County formally announced legal action against the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers over its plan to drain Detroit Lake before completing the turbidity analysis required under federal law.This issue affects drinking water, agriculture, recreation, fish populations, and the future of Santiam Canyon communities still recovering from the devastating 2020 wildfires. [](https://daniellebethell.cmail19.com/t/y-l-auldrut-hhlrhljhit-y/) I've been directly involved in these conversations because these are not abstract policy debates to me. They affect real families, real businesses, and entire Oregon communities that deserve to be heard before federal agencies move forward with decisions that could have lasting consequences.As I said at the meeting, any changes to Detroit Lake's water level must be grounded in data-backed science with meaningful protections in place for our downstream communities. This lawsuit seeks to address the Army Corps' lack of compliance with federal law and protect our local residents from potentially catastrophic results.This is exactly why I decided to run for Governor. [Can You Chip In Now?](https://daniellebethell.cmail19.com/t/y-l-auldrut-hhlrhljhit-j/) I'm not running to become part of the political class.
